halflog-handbook-text: A log split in half on the chopping block. Chop it again to split it into firewood. See also the Woodworking overview.
blockdesc-chopper-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically-powered chopper. Install the parts into it to assemble the machine.
chopper-need-arm: Install the arm before the head.
chopperpart-handbook-text: One of the parts used to build the automated chopper. Install it with rightmouse to assemble the machine.
chopperheadhalf-handbook-text: Half of an automated chopper head. Forge two halves of the same metal on an anvil, then join them with a hammer on the crafting grid into a finished head.
chopper-handbook-text: Place the chopper frame, then install its parts with rightmouse in any order: a drive, an arm and an ordinary chopping block as the bed, then a chopper head into the arm. Only the head can be taken back out, with Ctrl + rightmouse. The three mechanism parts are fixed once installed, so break the frame to recover them. Drive the assembled frame with an axle from a windmill or water wheel. Load a log or firewood, by hand with rightmouse or through a chute: each shaft revolution raises and drops the axe once, and the finished batch is ejected in front. The machine takes the same inputs and yields the same firewood and sticks as the hand chopping block, except that a whole log goes straight to firewood, skipping the half-log step. The metal the head is made of affects its durability. See also the Woodworking overview.
blockdesc-sawmill-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically-powered sawmill. Install the parts into it to assemble the machine.
sawmill-need-sash: Install the saw sash before the blades.
sawmill-need-crankshaft: Install the crankshaft before the flywheel.
sawmill-blades-installed: A blade kit is already installed.
sawmillpart-handbook-text: One of the parts used to build the automated sawmill. Install it with rightmouse to assemble the machine.
pitsaw-handbook-text: Used on a pair of sawhorses to rip logs into planks and debarked logs into support beams, faster than an ordinary saw. Forge a pit saw blade and haft it onto a stick. With the Toolsmith mod the saw is assembled on the tool workbench instead, and sharpness matters: a blunt saw rips slower, so keep it honed. See the Woodworking overview.
barkspud-handbook-text: Used on a pair of sawhorses to strip the bark off a log, turning it into a debarked log. It is the quickest of the three debarking tools. Forge a bark spud head and haft it onto a stick. With the Toolsmith mod the spud is assembled on the tool workbench instead, and sharpness matters: a blunt edge strips slower, so keep it honed. See the Woodworking overview.
choppingblock-handbook-text: Place a log, half-log or firewood on the block with rightmouse, then hold rightmouse with an axe to chop it. Take placed wood back with Ctrl + rightmouse. A log splits into two half-logs that drop off the block; put one back to split it into firewood, and firewood gives sticks. The block itself can be burned as fuel. See also the Woodworking overview.
sawhorse-handbook-text: Build a trestle with rightmouse: a stick, a second stick, then a length of rope. Set a second trestle directly beside the first (not diagonally), and the two lock into a working pair. Lay a log or debarked log on the pair with rightmouse, stand at either end and hold rightmouse with a pit saw to rip it lengthwise: a log gives planks, a debarked log gives support beams. An ordinary saw also works, at half speed. Keep holding and the pair feeds itself the next matching log from your inventory, so a whole stack flows through in one go. To strip bark instead, stand at the side rather than an end and hold rightmouse with a bark spud (fastest), an axe with a hammer in the offhand, or a knife (slowest). The debarked log drops out beside the pair, so lay it back to rip it into support beams. A log can be sawn or stripped, not both; whichever you begin first locks it in. Take the log back with Ctrl + rightmouse. It comes back whole while the work is barely started. Once you are well into it the wood is committed, and the same gesture (or breaking a trestle) discards it. See also the Woodworking overview.
sawmill-handbook-text: Place the sawmill frame, then install its parts with rightmouse in any order: a carriage, a saw sash, a crankshaft and feed levers, then a blade kit into the sash. Only the blade kit can be taken back out, with Ctrl + rightmouse. The four mechanism parts are fixed once installed, so break the frame to recover them. Drive the assembled frame with an axle from a windmill or water wheel. Feed a log or debarked log into the top, by hand with rightmouse or through a chute: a log gives planks, a debarked log gives support beams. The metal the blades are made of affects their durability. See also the Woodworking overview.
craftinginfo-woodworking-text: Raw wood is worked at several stations. A chopping block splits wood with an axe: a log first into two half-logs and then into firewood, and firewood into sticks. Beach driftwood is broken apart by hand: hold rightmouse to snap it into firewood and sticks, and larger pieces give more. A pair of sawhorses rips logs lengthwise with a pit saw: logs into planks, and debarked logs into support beams. The same sawhorses also strip bark: stand at the side and hold rightmouse with a bark spud, an axe with an offhand hammer, or a knife. An automated sawmill does the same ripping under mechanical power, hands-off and in a single pass. An automated chopper splits logs into firewood under mechanical power, one axe strike per shaft revolution. See each station's handbook page for how to build and use it.
blockinfo-sawmill-nopower: No power, connect a turning axle
blockinfo-chopper-nopower: No power, connect a turning axle
blockinfo-chopper-headdown: Axe down, waiting for it to lift

ingameerror-sawhorse-needsaw: You need a saw to rip a log here
ingameerror-sawhorse-needend: Stand at an end of the sawhorses to saw
ingameerror-sawhorse-needdebarktool: You need a knife, an axe with an offhand hammer, or a bark spud to strip bark here
ingameerror-sawhorse-needdebarktoolnokni: You need an axe with an offhand hammer, or a bark spud to strip bark here
ingameerror-sawhorse-needside: Stand at the side of the sawhorses to strip bark
ingameerror-sawhorse-lockeddebarking: This log is being stripped. Discard it (Ctrl + right-click) to saw instead
ingameerror-sawhorse-lockedsawing: This log is being sawn. Discard it (Ctrl + right-click) to strip bark instead
ingameerror-chopper-headdown: The axe is down, load the log once it lifts
iwsource-plank-text: Ripped lengthwise from a log on a pair of sawhorses with a pit saw, or on an automated sawmill. The crafting-grid saw recipe has been replaced by these stations. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-plank-text-also: Can also be ripped from a log on a pair of sawhorses with a pit saw, or on an automated sawmill, alongside the crafting grid. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-supportbeam-text: Ripped from a debarked log on a pair of sawhorses with a pit saw, or on an automated sawmill. The crafting-grid saw recipe has been replaced by these stations. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-supportbeam-text-also: Can also be ripped from a debarked log on a pair of sawhorses or an automated sawmill, alongside the crafting grid. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-firewood-text: Split from a log on a chopping block with an axe, or on an automated chopper. The crafting-grid firewood recipe has been replaced by the chopping block. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-firewood-text-also: Can also be split from a log on a chopping block with an axe, or on an automated chopper, alongside the crafting grid. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-stick-text: Also split from firewood on a chopping block with an axe, or by snapping beach driftwood apart by hand. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-log-text: Worked at the woodworking stations: split into firewood on a chopping block with an axe, or ripped into planks on a pair of sawhorses or an automated sawmill. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-logsection-text: Ripped into planks on a pair of sawhorses or an automated sawmill, or split into firewood on a chopping block. See the Woodworking overview.
iwsource-debarkedlog-text: Ripped into support beams on a pair of sawhorses or an automated sawmill, or split into firewood on a chopping block. See the Woodworking overview.
abilitydesc-sawyer: Increases the yield of planks and beams from sawing logs by {0}% and additional {1}% for each level at the forestry skill. Maxed out at {2}%.
abilitydesc-carefulsawyer: Sawing or debarking a log has a chance of {0}% and additional {1}% for each level at the forestry skill to not reduce the durability of your saw or bark tool. The chance is capped at {2}%.
abilitydesc-splitter: Increases the yield of firewood from splitting logs by {0}% and additional {1}% for each level at the forestry skill. Maxed out at {2}%.
abilitydesc-swifthands: Speeds up your rip-sawing on the sawhorses and your axe chopping by {0}% plus an additional {1}% for each forestry level, up to {2}%.
